records.title: Spain's Strangest Borders
records.script: Did you know Spain is the country with the strangest borders? On the map, it looks like Spain has only two land neighbors, France and Portugal. But in reality, there are many more. Just the border with France creates a few unusual oddities. For example, the town of Libya, which lies entirely within French territory, only 2 km from the border, but it is Spanish territory. This phenomenon is called an enclave. And moving further west, you'll find an even more surprising case, pheasant island. Long ago, Spain and France couldn't agree on how to divide the island because the border ran right through the middle. So, they decided to take turns owning it. For the first half of the year, the island belongs to Spain, and for the second half, the border shifts and it becomes French territory. There is also another neighbor hidden between Spain and France, and Pandora. It's one of the smallest countries in the world with a population of about 80,000 and almost half the size of New York City. But Spain has another hidden neighbor, and it's much larger, the United Kingdom. Even though Britain lies far to the north, it holds an overseas territory at the very southern tip of the Iberian Peninsula, Gibralar, which for centuries has been a point of dispute between Spain and the UK, as it controls access to the Mediterranean through the Straight of Gibralar. The strait itself divides two continents, Europe and Africa. But despite this, Spain is the only European country that shares a land border with Africa, thanks to three Spanish enclaves bordering Morocco, another unexpected neighbor. Two of them are the cities of Suda and Mala and the third is a tiny strip of land that was once an island but over time became connected to the mainland by a narrow istmas creating the shortest land border in the world just 85 m song.

records.title: What does the shortest border in the world really look like?
records.script: what is the shortest border on Earth in one of my older videos I said that the shortest was this 150 M border from Botswana to Zambia but I kind of lied because while this may be the shortest entire border between two countries it's not the single shortest border that title goes surprisingly to Spain and Morocco now you might be thinking what these countries are clearly separated by the Mediterranean Sea right how could they possibly share a border together well you see back in the early 1900s Spain used to control this little bit of Northern Morocco when they finally decided to give up this territory a couple parts were still left in Spanish possession regions like seuda and Malia but Spain also kept a few smaller pieces of land off Morocco's Coast including this small rock inhabited only by a couple dozen Spanish soldiers who are stationed there 24/7 still trying to hold on to this piece of land there's not actually any Roads connecting this piece of land to the rest of Morocco so any supplies that the Spanish need has to be brought in through helicopter this piece of land has become pretty famous over the years because this border only stretches about 85 M making it the shortest Border in the world

records.title: Noah Lyles won the 100m by point zero zero five seconds
records.script: do you see this what's happening here that's a hint that the photo finish system at the Olympics isn't actually giving us a photo and that's why it looks a little weird so these two Runners Cain Thompson and Noah ly both finished the 100 meter race with an official time of 9.79 seconds the announcer had called it for Thompson but it turned out his torso crossed that line 5,000th of a second after ly how do they know that well Omega which is the official timekeeper for the Olympics has a Finish Line camera that can capture 40,000 frames per second but instead of a normal camera it scans one vertical slice so this photo finish picture isn't capturing a moment in time it's capturing a place the finish line and what each body part of each Runner looked like as they were crossing it those vertical slices are then spread out horizontally by their time code so that the operator can mark their chests with a red line the ground is white because this camera is only capturing the finish line and the logos come from a billboard that only the Finish Line camera can read subscribe for more

records.title: 27 Years to Walk Around the World
records.script: This man has been walking for 27 years to become the only person in history to walk around the entire planet with just one rule. No transport of any kind. Carl Bushby began his journey in 1998 from the southern edge of Chile saying, I'll return home only on foot. After 2 years, he had crossed all of South America and faced his first major obstacle, the Darian Gap, one of the deadliest places on Earth with its impenetrable jungle, smugglers, and armed clashes between rebels and the military. As part of a group, Carl spent 50 days avoiding danger and somehow made it out alive. Panameanian soldiers even held him for 18 days before letting him continue his trek. It took 6 years to cross all of Central and North America and reach the Bearing Straight, which separates the two continents. After waiting for the straight to freeze, he and French traveler Dmitri Kefir became one of the first ever to cross it on foot despite drifting 80 km off course. Then he faced arrest in Russia and strict visa limits, which forced him to leave the route every 90 days and return to the exact same spot to continue his journey. As a result, his trek across Siberia, where temperatures dropped to minus50, stretched over 11 long years. When the world shut down during the pandemic and borders closed, Carl was stuck in Kazakhstan for 4 years and hit a dead end, the Caspian Sea. He couldn't go around it through Russia or Iran. So, he made one choice, to swim across. Using a support boat only for rest and sleep, he and American traveler Angela Maxwell crossed the Caspian Sea in 30 days, becoming the only people ever to do so. After nearly three decades, 25 countries, and 47,000 kilometers, Carl is now walking across Europe and is expected to finally return home by 2026.

records.title: The US-Canada Border Is 5,500 Miles of Pure Nonsense
records.script: Canada and the United States share the longest, straightest, possibly boringest border in the world. But, look closer, and there's plenty of bizarreness to be found. While these sister nations get along fairly well, they both want to make it really clear whose side of the continent is whose. And they've done this by carving a 20-foot wide space along the border. All five and a half thousand miles of it. With the exception of the rare New England town that predates national borders or the odd airport that needed extending, this space is the no-touching-zone between the countries and they're super serious about keeping it clear. It matters not if the no-touching-zone runs through hundreds of miles of virtually uninhabited Alaskan / Yukon wilderness. Those border trees, will not stand. Which might make you think this must be the longest, straightest deforested place in the world, but it isn't. Deforested: yes, but straight? Not at all. Sure it looks straight and on a map, and the treaties establishing the line say it's straight... but in the real world the official border is 900 lines that zig-zags from the horizontal by as much as several hundred feet. How did this happen? Well, imagine you're back in North America in the 1800s -- The 49th parallel has just been set as the national boundary and it's your job to make it real. You're handed a compass and a ball of string and told to carefully mark off the next 2/3rds of a continent. Don't mind that uncharted wilderness in the way: just keep the line straight. Yeah. Good luck. With that. The men who surveyed the land did the best they could and built over 900 monuments. They're in about as straight as you could expect a pre-GPS civilization to make, but it's not the kind of spherical / planar intersection that would bring a mathematician joy.
